meta.purpose: Master research database for NightFlow. Every feature must trace to a citation here. This file is read directly by the in-app 'The Science' tab (ResearchView).
meta.note: Effect-strength field is an honest label so the app never oversells weak evidence. Values: 'strong' (multiple RCTs/action-spectrum data), 'moderate' (replicated but limited), 'emerging' (single or small studies). Recency verified across 2020-2026 literature on 2026-07-06 — added Brown 2022 melanopic-EDI consensus, Nagare 2019 & Cajochen 2022 (brightness>color), and a 'limitations' counter-evidence topic (Cochrane 2023, Frontiers 2025).

topics.title: Blue Light & Melatonin
topics.summary: Short-wavelength light near 460-480nm is the single most potent suppressor of melatonin. This is the strongest evidence base in the whole app.
topics.implementationImpact: Presets must aggressively cut the 460-480nm band. This is the primary target of the warm-tint overlay and any gamma boost.

citations.title: Action Spectrum for Melatonin Regulation in Humans: Evidence for a Novel Circadian Photoreceptor
citations.authors: Brainard GC, Hanifin JP, Greeson JM, et al.
citations.keyFinding: Tested 8 wavelengths on 72 subjects; melatonin suppression peaked at 464nm, revealing a non-rod/non-cone circadian photoreceptor (melanopsin). The foundational action-spectrum study.

citations.title: An Action Spectrum for Melatonin Suppression: Evidence for a Novel Non-Rod, Non-Cone Photoreceptor System in Humans
citations.authors: Thapan K, Arendt J, Skene DJ
citations.keyFinding: Independent action spectrum peaking near 459nm, confirming Brainard. Two labs, same conclusion in the same year.

citations.title: Blue Light from Light-Emitting Diodes Elicits a Dose-Dependent Suppression of Melatonin in Humans
citations.authors: West KE, Jablonski MR, Warfield B, et al.
citations.keyFinding: LED blue light (~469nm) suppresses melatonin in a dose-dependent way at ecologically realistic intensities, directly relevant to screens.

topics.title: Green Light & Circadian Rhythm
topics.summary: The overlooked half of the problem. Green light (~555nm) suppresses melatonin nearly as much as blue at the START of exposure via the cone system, though the effect decays over hours. Standard blue-only filters miss this.
topics.implementationImpact: Presets must reduce the green channel too, not just blue. This is a core differentiator vs f.lux/Night Shift. Because green's effect decays with duration, aggressive green cut matters most in the first ~1-2 hours of wind-down.

citations.title: Spectral Responses of the Human Circadian System Depend on the Irradiance and Duration of Exposure to Light
citations.authors: Gooley JJ, Rajaratnam SMW, Brainard GC, Kronauer RE, Czeisler CA, Lockley SW
citations.keyFinding: At the start of exposure, 555nm green light suppressed melatonin as effectively as 460nm blue. Green's effect diminished over 6.5h (cone-driven) while blue stayed constant (melanopsin-driven). Justifies blocking green, not just blue.

citations.title: The Spectral Sensitivity of Human Circadian Phase Resetting and Melatonin Suppression to Light Changes Dynamically with Light Duration
citations.authors: St Hilaire MA, Gooley JJ, Khalsa SBS, et al.
citations.keyFinding: Confirms circadian spectral sensitivity shifts with exposure duration; multi-photoreceptor contribution means longer wavelengths matter more than a single blue-peak model predicts.

topics.title: Grayscale & Screen Compulsion
topics.summary: Removing color reduces how rewarding a screen feels, cutting compulsive use. Evidence is real but thinner than the light research — one strong field study plus a replication. The app should present this honestly as 'emerging', not settled science.
topics.implementationImpact: Grayscale is a behavioral (dopamine/reward) tool, distinct from the light layers. Schedule it later in the evening (Phase 3) to interrupt doomscrolling. Justifies the app-whitelist so color-critical work is exempt.

citations.title: True Colors: Grayscale Setting Reduces Screen Time in College Students
citations.keyFinding: 161 students; the 73 switched to grayscale for 8-10 days used their phones ~39.7 min/day less, with the biggest drops in web browsing and social media. First large-scale field test.

citations.title: Is Life Brighter When Your Phone Is Not? The Efficacy of a Grayscale Smartphone Intervention Addressing Digital Well-Being
citations.keyFinding: Replication showing grayscale reduces smartphone use, while cautioning effects on well-being are modest. Included for honesty about effect size.

topics.title: Overall Brightness (Lux) & Alertness
topics.summary: Beyond color, sheer intensity matters — and recent (2019-2022) work shows it matters MORE than color. Melatonin is suppressed at surprisingly low levels (~6 lux can halve it), bright light acutely raises alertness/cortisol, and warming color WITHOUT dimming is largely ineffective. This is the strongest justification for NightFlow's whole design.
topics.implementationImpact: The dimming overlay is not a nice-to-have — it is the highest-leverage layer. Every timeline phase MUST pair a color target with a real brightness reduction; a warm/red screen left bright still delays sleep. Modern target: aim the deep phases toward <=10 lux melanopic EDI (evening) trending to <=1 lux (bedtime) per Brown 2022.

citations.title: Sensitivity of the Human Circadian Pacemaker to Nocturnal Light: Melatonin Phase Resetting and Suppression
citations.authors: Zeitzer JM, Dijk DJ, Kronauer RE, Brown EN, Czeisler CA
citations.keyFinding: Dose-response study: ~6 lux was enough for 50% melatonin suppression in sensitive individuals; melatonin is far more light-sensitive than assumed. Basis for aggressive dimming.

citations.title: Recommendations for Daytime, Evening, and Nighttime Indoor Light Exposure to Best Support Physiology, Sleep, and Wakefulness in Healthy Adults
citations.authors: Brown TM, Brainard GC, Cajochen C, et al.
citations.keyFinding: Expert consensus using the modern SI-compliant metric (melanopic EDI, CIE S 026): evening <=10 lux melanopic EDI, sleep environment <=1 lux, daytime >=250 lux. The current gold-standard quantitative targets for the timeline's deep phases.

citations.title: Does the iPad Night Shift Mode Reduce Melatonin Suppression?
citations.authors: Nagare R, Plitnick B, Figueiro MG (Lighting Research Center)
citations.keyFinding: Warming screen color alone (Night Shift) did NOT meaningfully reduce melatonin suppression unless brightness was also lowered. Direct evidence that color-only apps are incomplete and that dimming is essential — the core rationale for NightFlow over f.lux/Night Shift.

citations.title: Influence of Evening Light Exposure on Polysomnographically Assessed Night-Time Sleep: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
citations.authors: Cajochen C, Stefani O, Schöllhorn I, Lang D, Chellappa SL
citations.keyFinding: Meta-analysis confirming evening light exposure measurably disrupts objectively-measured (PSG) sleep, with intensity a key driver. Raises the evidence for the brightness layer from single-study to meta-analytic.

topics.title: Limitations & Counter-Evidence (Honesty Section)
topics.summary: What the science does NOT firmly support. Shown in-app to prove NightFlow is honest, not hype. The strongest recent challenge: blue-light-FILTERING glasses show little proven benefit — but note the crucial distinction from what this app actually does.
topics.implementationImpact: Copy must never claim 'blue-light glasses science'. NightFlow's mechanism is REDUCING the melanopic light dose reaching the eye (dimming + heavy spectral shift + correct timing), which is better supported than the weak-filter-glasses approach the Cochrane review critiques. The Science tab should surface this section prominently.

citations.title: Blue-Light Filtering Spectacle Lenses for Visual Performance, Sleep, and Macular Health in Adults
citations.authors: Singh S, Downie LE, Anderson AJ, et al. (Cochrane Review)
citations.keyFinding: 17 RCTs, 619 participants: blue-light-FILTERING glasses showed no clear benefit for eye strain or sleep. Important caveat: these lenses block only a modest slice of blue and do NOT dim or heavily shift spectrum — unlike NightFlow's approach. Cited for honesty and to sharpen our positioning.

citations.title: Efficacy of Blue-Light Blocking Glasses on Actigraphic Sleep Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Crossover Trials
citations.keyFinding: Most recent meta-analysis on blue-blocking glasses; effects on actigraphic sleep are small and inconsistent. Reinforces that a weak spectral filter is not enough — the dose-reduction (dimming + timing) approach is what the stronger evidence supports.

topics.title: Timing of the Evening Wind-Down
topics.summary: Melatonin naturally begins to rise (Dim Light Melatonin Onset, DLMO) roughly 2-3 hours before natural sleep onset. Light exposure in this window is what delays the clock.
topics.implementationImpact: Sets the whole timeline structure: wind-down should begin ~2-3h before target bedtime, with the deepest filtering + grayscale concentrated in the final 1-2h. Drives the default phase offsets in CircadianEngine.

citations.title: Dim Light Melatonin Onset (DLMO): A Tool for the Analysis of Circadian Phase in Human Sleep and Chronobiological Disorders
citations.authors: Pandi-Perumal SR, Smits M, Spence W, et al.
citations.keyFinding: Establishes DLMO as the gold-standard marker of biological night onset, typically 2-3h before habitual sleep. Basis for anchoring the wind-down schedule to bedtime.

citations.title: The Dim Light Melatonin Onset Across Ages, Methodologies, and Sex and Its Relationship with Morningness/Eveningness
citations.authors: Crowley SJ, Eastman CI, et al.
citations.keyFinding: DLMO precedes sleep onset by ~2-3h on average and varies with chronotype, supporting a user-adjustable (not fixed) timeline.

topics.title: Red Light Safety
topics.summary: Long-wavelength red light (~620-670nm) has minimal impact on melatonin because it barely stimulates melanopsin. This is why the deepest 'Red Mode' preset is the safest for the final stretch before sleep.
topics.implementationImpact: Red Mode is the terminal phase of the timeline. Presets shift toward a near-pure red spectrum as bedtime approaches. Combined with heavy dimming and grayscale, it's the least alerting state a lit screen can be in.

citations.title: Comparative Effects of Red and Blue LED Light on Melatonin Levels During Three-Hour Exposure in Healthy Adults
citations.keyFinding: After 2h, red light allowed melatonin to recover to ~26.0 pg/mL while blue held it suppressed at ~7.5 pg/mL. Direct human evidence that red is far gentler on melatonin.

citations.title: Modeling the Influence of Nighttime Light on Melatonin Suppression in Humans: Milestones and Perspectives
citations.keyFinding: Review of melatonin action spectra confirming suppression falls off sharply above ~600nm; red wavelengths sit in the safe tail. Context for choosing the Red Mode target.
